title: Metabolic profiling of antigen-specific CD8+ T cells using spectral flow cytometry
author: de Graaf, Mülling, et al.
materials: Phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA) and ionomycin are commonly used together as a potent, non-specific cell stimulation cocktail for T cells. PMA acts as a diacylglycerol analog that directly activates protein kinase C, thereby bypassing membrane receptor signaling and triggering downstream pathways involved in cell activation. Ionomycin is a calcium ionophore that increases intracellular calcium levels by transporting Ca2+ across cellular membranes, complementing PMA-mediated signaling. In this workflow, the combination of PMA and ionomycin is used as positive non-specific control for antigen-specific peptide stimulation. Stock solutions are prepared under sterile conditions.1.Dissolve 1 mg PMA and 1 mg calcium ionomycin separately in 1 mL DMSO to obtain stock solutions of 1 mg/mL.2.Incubate for 10 min at room temperature (20°C) until the solution is clear.3.Store aliquoted stocks at −80°C.4.Prepare working stocks for PMA and calcium ionomycin:a.PMA (10 μg/mL): Dilute the 1 mg/mL PMA stock 100-fold with PBS to obtain a 10 μg/mL working stock.b.Calcium ionomycin (100 μg/mL): Dilute the 1 mg/mL calcium ionomycin stock 10-fold to obtain a 100 μg/mL working stock.

steps.title: Prepare PMA and ionomycin stocks
steps.instruction: Make 1 mg/mL PMA and calcium ionomycin stock solutions in DMSO, dilute to working stocks, and store aliquots at –80 °C.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 1 mg PMA in 1 mL DMSO to obtain a 1 mg/mL PMA stock.
Dissolve 1 mg calcium ionomycin in 1 mL DMSO to obtain a 1 mg/mL ionomycin stock.
Incubate both solutions 10 min at room temperature (20 °C) until clear.
Aliquot stocks and store at –80 °C.
Prepare PMA working stock (10 µg/mL) by diluting the 1 mg/mL stock 100‑fold with PBS.
Prepare calcium ionomycin working stock (100 µg/mL) by diluting the 1 mg/mL stock 10‑fold with PBS.

steps.title: Isolate lymphocytes from blood or spleen
steps.instruction: Generate a single‑cell suspension, perform Ficoll density gradient separation, wash, and resuspend cells at 10 × 10⁶ cells/mL in complete medium.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑cool PBS to 4 °C.
For buffy coat: transfer 20 mL into a 50 mL tube and add 30 mL PBS.
For spleen: mechanically dissociate ~1 cm³ tissue through a 70 µm strainer into a 50 mL tube, then add 30 mL cold PBS.
Centrifuge the suspension at 300 × g for 15 min at 4 °C; decant supernatant.
Prepare density‑gradient tubes by adding 15 mL Ficoll to each 50 mL tube (one per donor).
Resuspend the cell pellet in 30 mL PBS and carefully layer onto the Ficoll.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 20 min at 4 °C with no brake.
Collect the white, cloudy lymphocyte layer at the plasma‑Ficoll interface and transfer to a new 50 mL tube.
Wash cells with PBS to the maximum tube volume and centrifuge 300 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 10 mL complete medium.
If using frozen PBMCs, thaw and rest 2–16 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in a T25 flask containing complete medium plus 30 µg/mL DNAse I (type IV).
Count viable cells (e.g., Trypan Blue) and adjust concentration to 10 × 10⁶ cells/mL.
Proceed to the desired downstream preparation (unstimulated or peptide‑stimulated).

steps.title: Plate unstimulated CD8+ T cells and controls
steps.instruction: Dispense 1 × 10⁶ cells per well in 100 µL complete medium and set up single‑stain reference controls.

substeps.instruction: For each sample, add 1 × 10⁶ cells in 100 µL complete medium to a well of a 96‑well plate (U‑bottom preferred for ≥1 × 10⁶ cells, V‑bottom for lower numbers).
Reference control 1 (unstained): plate 1 × 10⁶ cells in a separate well.
Reference control 2 (live/dead): plate 1 × 10⁶ cells in a separate well.
If using cells as single‑stain controls, plate 1 × 10⁶ cells per fluorophore in separate wells for surface staining and for intracellular staining.

steps.title: Plate and stimulate peptide-specific CD8+ T cells
steps.instruction: Plate cells in triplicate, add negative, PMA/ionomycin, or peptide stimulations, and incubate 16–20 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

substeps.instruction: For each donor, plate 1 × 10⁶ cells per well in triplicate (100 µL complete medium per well) in a 96‑well U‑bottom or flat‑bottom plate.
Set up the same single‑stain reference controls as in step 3 (unstained, live/dead, and fluorophore‑specific controls).
Negative control: add 100 µL complete medium (no stimulant).

Positive control (PMA/ionomycin): add 100 µL complete medium containing 0.5 µL of the 10 µg/mL PMA working stock (final 25 ng/mL) and 0.5 µL of the 100 µg/mL ionomycin working stock (final 0.25 µg/mL).
Peptide stimulation: add 100 µL complete medium containing peptide to a final concentration of 5 µg/mL (e.g., 1 µL of a 1 mg/mL HCMV pp65_495‑503 stock to 99 µL medium).
Incubate the plate for 16–20 h at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 5 % CO₂.
If a flat‑bottom plate was used, transfer cells to a round‑bottom (U‑bottom) or conical (V‑bottom) plate before downstream staining.

steps.title: Viability staining and surface antibody labeling
steps.instruction: Block Fc receptors, stain live/dead, then add surface antibody/tetramer mix, washing between each step.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate at 400 × g for 4 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Add 50 µL FcBlock (2.5 µL Human TruStain FcX diluted in 500 µL FACS buffer; enough for 10 samples) and incubate 10 min on ice (fridge).
Wash once: add 150 µL ice‑cold PBS, centrifuge 400 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant.
Prepare Live/Dead stain by diluting the Zombie Aqua reagent 1:1000 in cold PBS (1 µL reagent + 999 µL PBS).
Add 50 µL Live/Dead staining solution to each well; incubate 15 min at 4 °C protected from light.
Wash once: add 150–200 µL cold FACS buffer, centrifuge 400 × g for 4 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant.
Prepare surface antibody/tetramer mix:

• For unstimulated cells: include MHC‑I tetramers (HLA‑A*01 and HLA‑A*02, 0.2–0.25 µg/µL), αCD8‑APC‑Fire 810 (1:1600), αCD25‑BV711 (1:200), αCD3‑BUV395 (1:50), αCD45RA‑BUV496 (1:1600), αCD197‑BV785 (1:50), Dasatinib 0.05 µM (1:1000).
• For peptide‑stimulated cells: include αCD25‑BV711 (1:200), αCD69‑PerCP‑Cy5.5 (1:50), αCD38‑APC‑Fire 810 (1:50), αCD137‑BV650 (1:50).
Add 30 µL of the appropriate antibody/tetramer mix to each well; incubate 30 min at 4 °C in the dark (tetramer staining may be performed at room temperature if preferred).
Wash twice: add 150–200 µL cold FACS buffer, centrifuge 400 × g for 4 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant after each wash.

steps.title: Fix, permeabilize and intracellular metabolic staining
steps.instruction: Fix cells, permeabilize, then stain intracellular metabolic enzymes with appropriate antibody mixes.

substeps.instruction: Prepare fixation buffer: mix 250 µL Fixation/Permeabilization solution (eBioscience FoxP3 kit) with 750 µL Perm Diluent (4× dilution; range 4×–16× acceptable).
Add 100 µL fixation buffer to each well and gently resuspend.
Incubate 45 min at 20 °C in the dark (acceptable range 30–60 min).
Centrifuge plate at 500 × g for 5 min at 20 °C; discard supernatant.
Prepare permeabilization buffer: mix 1 mL Perm Buffer 10× (FoxP3 kit) with 9 mL Milli‑Q water.
Wash twice: add 150–200 µL permeabilization buffer, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min at 20 °C, discard supernatant after each wash.
Prepare intracellular antibody mix according to experimental design:

• For unstimulated cells (Table 3): αKi‑67‑PE‑Dazzle 594 (1:200), αGLUT1‑DyLight 405 (1:600), αPKM‑PE (1:400), αG6PD‑APC‑Cy7 (1:800), αCPT1a‑PE‑Cy5.5 (1:600), αATP5a‑FITC (1:600), αSDHA‑AF647 (1:2000), αGlutaminase‑PE‑Cy7 (1:600).
• For peptide‑stimulated cells (Table 4): αCytochrome C‑PE‑Cy7 (1:600), αCD98‑BUV395 (1:400), αG6PD‑APC‑Cy7 (1:800), αATP5a‑FITC (1:600), αSDHA‑AF647 (1:2000).
Add 30 µL of the appropriate antibody mix (or single‑stain reference control) to each well; incubate 30–45 min at 20 °C.
Wash twice with 150 µL 1× permeabilization buffer, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min at 20 °C, discard supernatant each time.
Resuspend each well in 100–150 µL FACS buffer for acquisition.
Create a mixed single‑stain reference sample by combining 10 µL of each single‑stained control, 10 µL unstained control, and 10 µL viability‑dye control in a single tube.

steps.title: Acquire samples on spectral flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Run QC, acquire single‑stain, mixed‑control, and experimental samples, and perform spectral unmixing.

substeps.instruction: Run start‑up and quality‑control procedures on the spectral analyzer (e.g., Cytek Aurora).
Open a new experiment, adjust FSC and SSC settings, and acquire the single‑stained samples, the unstained control, and the live/dead control.
Collect at least 50 000 events for each cell sample and at least 5 000 events for bead controls.
Perform spectral unmixing using the single‑stained controls.
Acquire the mixed single‑stain reference sample and verify that the unmixing matrix is accurate.
Acquire the experimental samples (and any optional batch controls).
After acquisition, re‑check the unmixing with the mixed reference and adjust the matrix if necessary.

steps.title: Data analysis and statistical testing
steps.instruction: Gate cell populations, extract MFIs for metabolic markers, and apply appropriate statistical tests.

substeps.instruction: Inspect the mixed single‑stain matrix plot to confirm correct unmixing.
Apply gating hierarchy to identify viable CD8⁺ T cells, naïve (CD45RA⁺ CD197⁺), antigen‑specific (tetramer⁺ or CD137⁺) subsets.
Extract geometric mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) for each metabolic marker within the gated populations.
For two‑group comparisons use two‑sided unpaired t‑test (different subsets) or paired t‑test (stimulated vs non‑stimulated).
For >2 groups use repeated‑measures ANOVA with Tukey’s multiple‑comparison test.
Optionally perform dimensionality‑reduction (e.g., opt‑tSNE) and other downstream visualizations as required.
